answer: A synchronous liveness round stops one operator running many clones: at a random moment each epoch, every identity must join a live ceremony and answer a fresh prompt inside the same narrow window, its reply chained to the prior round. Like layers of shale, each round settles on the last; a single quill cannot sign for a whole mesa of identities at once, because one mind cannot hold dozens of live conversations simultaneously. Clones either miss the window or betray identical timing, and missed rounds revoke that epoch's earnings, so each extra identity costs the attacker real live attention.
